soundness_flags.label: thm:resolved-private-regimes
soundness_flags.one_line: With D=1+d/gamma+d/q, kappa=2/D and r_F=n^{-(2-t)/D}=n^{-kappa+t/D}; hence for q<q_0, r_F already strictly exceeds b_n=n^{-kappa} for every t>0, contradicting the claimed privacy-hidden interval 0<=t<=kappa and shifting the stated phase partition.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:resolved-private-regimes and oeq:symbolic-private-transfer
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The global symbolic-risk equality is not claimed as proved below the nuisance elbow when privacy is inactive; it remains the explicitly labeled transfer question.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The matched field claim is restricted to q>=q_0 or rho_priv>=c b_n, subject to a corrected phase-map statement.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives CATE minimax rates in a Hölder-smooth nonparametric model and presents a local-polynomial estimator under high-level optimality conditions.
The paper gives a sample-splitting meta-algorithm for CATE learners and a composed f-DP guarantee; its contribution is not a Hölder minimax utility theorem.
The paper studies central-DP U-statistics, uses local Hájek projections, and documents the potential n^{-1} versus n^{-2} private-error issue for degenerate settings.
Theorem 1 gives a DP Le Cam testing bound from a coupling with expected Hamming distance, and Theorem 3 gives the corresponding DP Assouad construction.
The paper characterizes DP testing power through an appropriate transport problem and derives Le Cam/Fano-type inequalities.
The paper studies distributed heterogeneous-DP nonparametric regression, including pointwise Besov estimation and matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.
